questions.question: A team wants to add a capability beyond MCP's core primitives without colliding with anyone else who had the same idea. What must its extension identifier include?
options: A checksum computed over the settings object it carries
A numeric version suffix placed right after the name
A mandatory vendor prefix before the slash and name
A leading underscore marking the field as experimental
questions.explanation: Extension identifiers follow vendor-prefix/extension-name, and unlike an ordinary _meta key the prefix is mandatory, so unrelated vendors and official extensions never collide on the same name.

questions.question: Under the 2026-07-28 revision, where does a client declare which extensions it wants active for one particular tools/call request?
options: In the initialize request's capabilities, sent once when the connection opens
In an Mcp-Extensions header attached to that same HTTP request
In a separate extensions negotiate call sent immediately before it
In that request's own _meta, under clientCapabilities extensions
questions.explanation: There is no initialize handshake or session in 2026-07-28; a client declares its extensions fresh in _meta on every request, under io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.extensions.

questions.question: A client's request declares extensions A and B. The server's capabilities list extensions B and C. Which extension is active for this call?
options: Only B, because it is the one both sides named
None of them, because activation needs a separate confirmation step
A, B, and C, because declaring any of them activates all three
Only A, because the client is the one asking for behavior
questions.explanation: An extension is active only when both the client's declared capabilities and the server's own capabilities name the same identifier, so the negotiated set here is just B.

questions.question: A tool has no meaningful core-only behavior and only works with one specific mandatory extension active. A client calls it without that extension declared. What does a conformant server return?
options: A JSON-RPC error -32001, an old tool-failure code
A JSON-RPC error -32021, naming the extension it still needs
A JSON-RPC error -32601, because the method itself is unknown
A normal result with isError true and no other detail
questions.explanation: A request that needs a capability, including an extension, that its own clientCapabilities did not declare is refused with MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError, -32021, naming what was missing in data.requiredCapabilities.

questions.question: Before Core Maintainers will review a new official extension proposal at all, what must already exist?
options: A public vote among every registered MCP server operator
A full year of production traffic logged against the draft
A working reference implementation of it in an official SDK
A completed client support matrix showing every major client
questions.explanation: An Extensions Track SEP must already have a reference implementation in an official SDK before the Core Maintainers will review it, unlike a Standards Track SEP.

questions.question: An official extension's maintainers need to remove a field that existing implementations depend on. What does the framework require them to do?
options: Ask every client vendor to update on the very same day
Wait for a twelve month deprecation window like a core feature
Publish the change quietly, since extensions evolve without core review
Ship it under a new identifier instead of the existing one
questions.explanation: A breaking change such as removing a field must ship under a new extension identifier, for example an added v2 suffix, so implementations still declaring the old one keep the old, unmodified behavior.
